questions.q: Per this lesson, what does "gasless" actually mean?
options: The user doesn't need to hold the native gas token to pay for the transaction themselves — someone else covers it; gas itself still has a real cost
The transaction consumes zero blockspace and has no cost to anyone
The contract executes without using any gas because it's marked view
The user pays gas in a different cryptocurrency chosen at random
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that gas doesn't disappear — gasless means the user isn't the one who has to hold and spend the token, not that the cost vanishes.

questions.q: In the meta-transaction pattern described in this lesson, what does the user actually sign?
options: An off-chain intent describing what they want to happen, not a transaction itself
A raw, unsigned Ethereum transaction that they then broadcast themselves
A SIWE login message that doubles as transaction authorization
Nothing — the relayer signs on the user's behalf using a shared key
questions.explain: The lesson draws this parallel directly to SIWE: the user signs an intent off-chain, and the relayer is the one who turns it into a real, gas-paying transaction.

questions.q: Why can't a contract receiving a relayed call just use `msg.sender` directly to authorize the action, per this lesson?
options: Inside a relayed call, msg.sender is the relayer's address, not the original user's, so checking it directly would authorize the relayer instead
msg.sender is always the zero address inside any Solidity function
Solidity does not allow msg.sender to be read inside external functions
msg.sender only works correctly when ERC-2771 is NOT used
questions.explain: The lesson explains this is exactly the problem ERC-2771's trusted-forwarder pattern solves — msg.sender would otherwise be the relayer, not the user whose intent was signed.

questions.q: What does `_msgSender()` do inside a contract that inherits OpenZeppelin's `ERC2771Context`, according to this lesson?
options: It returns the original user's address, extracted from calldata appended by the trusted forwarder, instead of the relayer's address
It returns the contract's own address
It always returns the zero address for security reasons
It is identical to msg.sender in every situation, with no special behavior
questions.explain: The lesson explains _msgSender() is the ERC-2771-aware override that recovers the real user's address from the forwarder's appended calldata, replacing raw msg.sender.

questions.q: What real cost and risk does this lesson attach to operating a relayer?
options: The relayer pays real gas out of its own funded wallet and must decide which requests to sponsor, since an open relayer accepting any signed intent drains its own funds
Relayers are provided for free indefinitely by the Ethereum Foundation with no cost to the app
Relayers eliminate the need for any signature verification whatsoever
There is no real cost; the lesson describes relaying as entirely free to operate
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that gasless UX for the user means somebody — the app, a sponsor, a treasury — pays real gas, and that cost must be budgeted and rate-limited like any other operating expense.
